- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., +1.00) and news volume is high, model tends to overreact — cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., -0.67+ consecutive change) and price is trending up, model often fails to reverse — reduce forecast by 5–10% of recent gain.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots — apply a “cool-down” rule: subtract 2–5% of the spike magnitude from next forecast if sentiment stabilizes or turns neutral.
- When sentiment is flat or mildly positive but news volume is low, model tends to underestimate — add 1–3% to forecast if recent 3–5 days show no strong trend.
- If sentiment change is negative but price is still rising, model often ignores sentiment — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per negative sentiment change unit.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates when sentiment is volatile — use sentiment volatility as a multiplier (e.g., if sentiment swings ±0.5+ in last 5 days, reduce forecast by 2–4%).
